label: UniFi LTE Backup Pro
description: UniFi LTE Backup Pro - a failover modem for a UniFi gateway: 2x 1G RJ45, one PoE-in port (whose output is not used) and one PoE+ passthrough output at up to 15.4 W, plus an LTE Cat 4 radio (150/50 Mbps) with an internal antenna pair and an RP-SMA connector for an external one.
notes: Vendor figures: **(2) GbE RJ45 ports**, **LTE Category 4 radio** (MIMO 2x2, **download 150 Mbps / upload 50 Mbps**), **(1) PoE in (PoE output not used)** and **(1) PoE passthrough output (requires a PoE+ switch)**, 48V 0.5A PoE adapter or a UniFi PoE switch, supported voltage range 44-57V DC, **max power consumption 8.5 W excluding PoE passthrough**, **max PoE passthrough wattage per port 15.4 W**. Cited 2026-11-19: https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/integrations/u-lte-backup-pro (200, 624,978 B) prints every row above; https://dl.ui.com/ds/u-lte-backup-pro_ds.pdf (200, application/pdf, 329,546 B, 2 pp, text layer) prints the same census plus the 15.4W footnote; https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/u-lte-backup-pro (200, 402,625 B, landed on its collection URL) repeats the spec table and names the output port "PoE+ GbE Port (Passthrough)". The Cat 4 link is modelled at 150M - the vendor prints 150 Mbps download, not just the category, so this is the same figure as the UMR and the other Cat 4 rows rather than a class guess. A management detail, not a port: the unit also carries a 1.54" LCM display and a factory-reset button.

poe.note: 15.4 W, the vendor's "Max. PoE passthrough wattage per port" - published as per-port output, and this box has exactly one passthrough port, so it is also its whole budget. The footnote on both the tech-spec row and the datasheet is "Requires a PoE+ switch": the 8.5 W the unit itself draws plus 15.4 W passed through exceeds what an 802.3af source can deliver, which is why the upstream port must be Type 2.
